finding: Semantic JSON canonicalization is unsafe when duplicate member names are allowed to reach an ordinary parser, because parser-specific collapse can erase the ambiguity before hashing or attestation.

source_status.claim: Object member names should be unique; receiver behavior for duplicates is unpredictable.
I-JSON objects must not contain duplicate member names.
JCS input is constrained to I-JSON and therefore requires unique property names.

verified_behaviors: duplicate members rejected before parser collapse
same member name permitted in distinct object scopes
non-finite conversion and trailing content rejected

evidence_strength: primary-specification-derived implementation with deterministic local tests and committed source
uncertainty: The implementation has not yet been differential-tested against multiple independent streaming parsers.
Byte decoding is assumed to occur before this boundary; malformed UTF-8 byte handling is not implemented here.
This parser does not itself produce RFC 8785 canonical output.
falsification_route: Run a corpus containing duplicate names, escaped-equivalent names, malformed strings, extreme numbers, and deep nesting through this module and at least two independent strict parsers; any accepted ambiguous object or divergent accepted value falsifies the boundary.
